rows.notes: The cited document is a literature review (titled 'Review', Ecological Indicators 2022) analysing 22 published studies that combine remote sensing and machine learning to estimate soil quality indicators. It reports no original data, experiment, survey or validated model run of its own; the 'model' it proposes (Section 6.4, Fig. 1) is a conceptual scheme whose validation is explicitly left as a recommended future case study. Hence Q1 is 'no' and all subsequent questions are 'no'. The claim that Diaz-Gonzalez et al. 'used RS and ML to estimate soil quality' misattributes the reviewed studies' work to the review itself.

Same document: a review, not a primary study (Q1 'no'). The statement that the ML output is used by crop management to adjust practices and thereby improve crop yield (Section 7, Fig. 1) is a description of a proposed conceptual scheme, not a measured result. The review itself notes (Section 6.3) that none of the analysed works reports how the generated information was used by crop managers to improve procedures, and that validation of the proposed model remains to be done. No own evidence on crop yield effects exists in this document.

notes: The document is a narrative review of 22 studies on ML and RS for soil quality indicator estimation; it contains no primary data. Text appears complete (sections 1-7 plus references).
